ui.title: You do not need to know what you want to become.
ui.description: Tell us what interests you, how you work, what feels like a strength, and what matters around you. Xtara will turn those answers into Career Directions to explore.
ui.processingDescription: We are looking for patterns across your interests, strengths, personality, values, and family context—not calculating a perfect-career score.
ui.privacy: Your answers remain temporary until you create an account to save them.
ui.exitDescription: Leave this assessment? You can return and continue later.
ui.noQuestions: No questions are available for this journey.

gradeQuestion.label: Which grade are you currently studying in?
gradeQuestion.description: Your grade changes the detail and next steps in the assessment. It does not limit the directions you can explore.

questions.label: Which activities make you curious, even if you have never tried them?
questions.description: Curiosity is a starting point, not proof that you should choose a related career.

options.label: Sing, play music, perform, or entertain
Draw, design, write, film, or tell a story
Build an app, game, website, or digital tool
Make, repair, cook, grow, or improve something
Help someone understand or improve their health
Investigate a question through facts or experiments
Plan an event, project, budget, or small venture
Understand a community problem and help solve it

questions.label: Which kinds of activities have you actually tried and enjoyed?
questions.description: This helps us separate curiosity from real experience. Having little experience is completely normal.

options.label: Art, music, writing, performance, or content creation
Puzzles, science investigations, coding, or research
Building, repairing, cooking, crafts, gardening, or practical work
Teaching, explaining, supporting, or caring for someone
Leading, planning, selling, coordinating, or taking responsibility
I have not had enough opportunities to know yet

questions.label: Which of these feel like strengths today?
questions.description: You can choose something that comes naturally or something you have developed through practice.

options.label: Expressing an idea, feeling, or story
Understanding how or why something works
Learning by doing, making, or fixing
Listening, explaining, or helping someone understand
Noticing what people need and supporting them
Taking responsibility and bringing people or tasks together
I am still discovering my strengths

questions.label: What makes you think these may be strengths?
questions.description: Marks can be useful evidence, but they are not the only evidence.

options.label: I continue practising even when it is difficult
I have made or completed something using it
A teacher, friend, or family member noticed it
People trust me with related responsibilities
My schoolwork or marks show it
It is mainly a feeling; I have not tested it yet
I do not have clear evidence yet

questions.label: When something feels like a weakness, what is usually happening?
questions.description: A low mark, low confidence, limited exposure, and genuine dislike mean different things.

options.label: I have tried it and usually do not enjoy it
I worry that I will get it wrong
My marks are lower than I want
I have not had enough chance to try it properly
The way I learned it did not work well for me
It is difficult, but I want to improve
I am not sure yet

questions.label: Your class starts a new group project. What would you naturally do first?
questions.description: Choose the response closest to what you normally do—not what sounds impressive.

options.label: Suggest interesting ideas
Understand the problem and gather information
Create a plan and divide the work
Start making a first version
Make sure everyone is heard
Observe for a while before choosing a role

questions.label: When you face a new problem, what helps you move forward?

options.label: Find facts and understand the rules
Try something and learn from what happens
Discuss it with other people
Imagine several unusual possibilities
Break it into smaller steps

questions.label: After spending time with a group of people, how do you usually feel?

options.label: More energetic and ready for more
It depends on the people and activity
I usually need quiet time to recharge

questions.label: Something important does not work the first time. What are you most likely to do?

options.label: Try again in a different way
Find out exactly why it failed
Ask someone for help or feedback
Take a break and return when I am ready
I often lose confidence and need encouragement

questions.label: What would you want your future work to give you?
questions.description: Choose what matters to you today. Your answers can change as you learn more.

options.label: Freedom to create or express ideas
A clear way to help people
Difficult problems and continuous learning
Visible and practical results
Responsibility and influence
Stability and a reliable income
Recognition and respect
Time and flexibility outside work

questions.label: How do career conversations usually feel in your family?
questions.description: Family guidance matters. We keep it separate from your strengths so it can support a better conversation rather than decide your potential.

options.label: My family is open to different possibilities
My family has preferred careers, but we can discuss them
My family strongly prefers a particular direction
My family wants to help but is unsure about the options
We have not really discussed careers yet
I prefer not to answer

questions.label: What does your family usually consider important for your future?
questions.description: These priorities will help with later pathway conversations; they do not change your career-direction signals.

options.label: Job stability
Strong earning potential
Social recognition or professional status
Staying near family
A manageable education duration
The student’s genuine interest
I am not sure

questions.label: Which kinds of work have you seen closely through family or people you know?
questions.description: Exposure can make some careers feel more familiar. It should not close unfamiliar possibilities.

options.label: Healthcare or wellbeing
Technology, engineering, or skilled trades
Business, finance, sales, or family enterprise
Education, government, law, or public service
Arts, media, design, or entertainment
Science, research, agriculture, or environment
Other kinds of work
I have had limited exposure to different careers

questions.label: Overall, how much opportunity have you had to explore your interests?
questions.description: Limited opportunity is not a weakness. It tells Xtara how certain or tentative the guidance should be.

options.label: Very little so far
I have tried a few related activities
I regularly take part in related activities

grade8.label: Where have you had chances to discover new interests?
grade8.description: Having few opportunities is not a weakness; it simply means your directions should remain broad.

options.label: School clubs, events, labs, or competitions
Home, family work, hobbies, or responsibilities
Sports, arts, community groups, or volunteering
Online videos, courses, games, or communities
I have had very few chances so far

grade9.label: Which experiences have helped you understand yourself better?
grade9.description: This is about exposure, not achievement.

options.label: A personal or school project
A conversation with someone about their work
A club, competition, workshop, sport, or volunteering activity
Helping with family work or responsibilities
I have not had these experiences yet

grade10.label: Which Grade 10 decision feels most urgent?

options.label: Understanding which subjects to continue
Comparing streams or study routes
Keeping several future options open
Preparing for a conversation with my family or school

grade10.label: Which subjects currently give you energy or confidence?
grade10.description: Subjects are one piece of evidence, not a permanent limit on what you can become.

options.label: Mathematics
Science
Languages
Social science
Arts or design
Computing
Commerce or economics
I am still discovering this

grade11.label: What would help you explore your next steps during Grade 11?
grade11.description: Use your current subjects as context, not a limit on your interests.

options.label: Connecting my current subjects to careers
Trying a project or talking to someone about their work
Understanding alternative study routes
Discussing my options with a teacher or family member

grade12.label: What would help you prepare for life after Grade 12?
grade12.description: Compare possible routes; this assessment does not decide your eligibility.

options.label: Comparing degrees, diplomas, training or apprenticeships
Checking current entry requirements and application dates
Understanding costs, location and available support
Discussing my options before choosing a route

creativeExpression.title: Creating and sharing ideas
creativeExpression.description: You may enjoy expressing ideas through stories, sound, images, or performance.

analysis.title: Solving problems
analysis.description: You may enjoy asking why, finding patterns, testing ideas, or making things work.

making.title: Learning by doing
making.description: You may learn well by building, repairing, making, or trying something yourself.

communication.title: Explaining and listening
communication.description: You may enjoy listening, explaining, teaching, or helping an idea make sense.

care.title: Helping people
care.description: You may notice what people need and enjoy work that improves someone’s life.

organizing.title: Planning and taking responsibility
organizing.description: You may enjoy bringing people, tasks, and plans together to finish something.

socialEnergy.title: Working with people
socialEnergy.description: Being with a group may give you energy when everyone shares a goal.

reflective.title: Thinking before responding
reflective.description: You may like time to observe and understand before you answer.

structured.title: Following a clear plan
structured.description: Clear steps and responsibilities may help you work well.

flexible.title: Trying and adjusting
flexible.description: You may like trying an idea and changing your approach as you learn.

collaborative.title: Working together
collaborative.description: You may think and work well by discussing ideas with other people.

independent.title: Working on your own
independent.description: You may like having space to focus and find your own answer.

practical.title: Learning by doing
practical.description: Trying something yourself may help you learn more than hearing an explanation.

conceptual.title: Thinking about ideas
conceptual.description: You may enjoy seeing how ideas connect and understanding why things happen.

persistence.title: Keeping going
persistence.description: You may continue when something is difficult if the result matters to you.

adaptive.title: Changing your approach
adaptive.description: You may work differently depending on the people, goal, and situation.

responsibility.title: Following through
responsibility.description: Other people may trust you to complete an important task.

family.open: Your family appears open to exploration.
family.preferred: Your family has preferred ideas, with room for discussion.
family.strong: Your family has strong ideas about your future. Their view is shown separately from your own interests.
family.uncertain: Your family wants to help but may need clearer career and education information.
family.notDiscussed: Career conversations have not really started at home yet.
family.preferNot: You chose not to share this. It does not change your Career Directions.

weakness.dislike: Some difficult areas may reflect genuine dislike after experience.
weakness.confidence: Low confidence may be affecting how you judge some abilities.
weakness.marks: Marks show only part of what you can do.
weakness.exposure: You may not know whether you enjoy something until you have a chance to try it.
weakness.teaching: The way something was taught may have affected your experience of it.
weakness.improve: You are willing to improve in areas that currently feel difficult.
weakness.notSure: You are still learning what difficulty means for you.

technology.title: Technology

health.title: Health
health.description: Help people stay healthy, recover, and live well.

science.title: Science
science.description: Ask questions, test ideas, and learn how things work.

business.title: Business
business.description: Turn ideas into useful products, services, and organisations.

design.title: Design and Media
design.description: Create clear, useful, and engaging experiences and stories.

society.title: Education and Society
society.description: Teach, support communities, and help solve public problems.
